headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while Windsurf can execute and auto-act on content, creating a dangerous default trust chain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and app content, while Windsurf can consume workspace files and MCP/API content. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled text from A can reach B as instructions. The pathway is not proven by a shared channel, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content is copied into Windsurf workspace files or MCP inputs
IF Windsurf treats imported file text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of model-generated text into agent prompts
Use a separate review-only folder for any A outputs
Add a provenance banner to imported files
Turn off MCP servers for untrusted content
requires-engineering: enforce instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files, and ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code while Windsurf reads workspace files. If the same workspace or synced files contain sensitive material, both agents can access it. The profiles do not show uncontrolled third-party exfiltration, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF the same sensitive workspace is opened in both agents
IF uploaded files or screenshots contain secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared workspaces
Use separate OS accounts or profiles
Redact secrets before upload
Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; ChatGPT Desktop can read filesystem and app context but has no write capability. The pair can still conflict through shared files and git state because B can mutate what A reads, and B supports multiple instances via local filesystem. This is a dangerous default write/read overlap.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-executes or commits changes while ChatGPT Desktop is reading the same files
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Lock the workspace during edits
requires-engineering: add file-locking or branch arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce file- and app-derived outputs that Windsurf may treat as actionable code or instructions, and Windsurf can then execute shell commands or modify git state. That creates a default trust chain from A to B with potentially irreversible downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses ChatGPT Desktop output as authoritative without manual review
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or command approval is bypassed
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Ask ChatGPT Desktop for citations before acting
Use a checklist for any generated commands
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Windsurf handles workspace files and model-provider keys. If regulated data or secrets are present in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency ambiguity. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents' workspaces
IF organizational policy requires distinct retention or residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review vendor retention settings
Avoid storing secrets in workspace files
Use separate projects for regulated work
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
